title: The AI boom runs on metal. A two-year-old startup just raised $310m to mine it, autonomously, on US soil.
excerpt: Mariana Minerals raised $310m at a $1.5bn valuation to run US copper and lithium mines with its own AI software, betting the AI boom needs domestic metal.
content_html:
People tell the AI boom as a story about chips and models. Underneath it is metal. Every data centre, chip, power line and robot starts with copper and a handful of other minerals. The United States has quietly lost control of where they come from. A two-year-old startup just raised $310m to change that.

Mariana Minerals is not selling software to miners. It owns and runs the mines itself, using its own AI stack, it announced. Khosla Ventures led the Series B, with a16z and Breakthrough Energy returning. It takes the company’s total capital to about $400m, at a $1.5bn valuation, Fortune first reported.

The founders are an unusual mix. Chief executive Turner Caldwell ran Tesla’s metals and minerals team. His co-founders came from machine learning at Affirm and from energy project finance. That blend is the whole pitch. Fuse mining execution, software and capital, they argue, and you can build a mine in half the usual time.

Copper, lithium and a China problem

The urgency is geopolitical. China dominates global mining. It processes as much as 90% of the world’s critical minerals. For the rare-earth magnets in phones and weapons, that rises to 92%. AI is driving metal demand to unprecedented levels. That dependence is now a national-security problem, not just an economic one.

Mariana’s answer is two US sites. Copper One is an idled Utah mine Mariana bought last year. It restarted under autonomous software in four months, and is ramping toward 50,000 tonnes of refined copper a year. Lithium One in Texas aims to pull battery-grade lithium from oil-and-gas wastewater, with production targeted for 2027.

Copper is the tell. It is the chokepoint for electrification, and the AI-era grid is straining for it. “You cannot lead in the AI century without a domestic supply chain,” said Travis Kalanick. The former Uber boss now runs a robotics firm. It is the same logic pulling money into energy and grid hardware.

Software can’t dig the hole

The backer list is the signal. Alongside a16z and Khosla sit BHP, one of the world’s largest miners, and In-Q-Tel, the CIA’s venture arm. That is venture, industry and national security betting on one thesis. Whoever automates mining fastest helps decide who wins the AI build-out, and who stays dependent on China.

The caution comes built into the business. This is not SaaS. It is construction crews, processing plants and commodity prices, none of which software can conjure away. Copper One still has to scale an existing operation. Lithium One still has to bring a brand-new facility into commercial production. Both can slip.

Vinod Khosla frames the gap plainly. The minerals are there; the missing pieces, he says, are the will and the AI to extract them autonomously. Mariana wants ten commercial projects in ten years, each one training the software for the next. It is an elegant flywheel on a slide, and a very hard thing to build in the ground.

For now the money has decided the thesis is worth $1.5bn. The proof will not come in demos or decks. It will come in tonnes of copper and lithium, on schedule and at a cost that undercuts the incumbents. That is the number the next round has to beat.

content_html_zh:
人们将人工智能的繁荣描述为一个关于芯片和模型的故事。 它下面是金属。 每个数据中心、芯片、电力线和机器人都始于铜和少量其他矿物。 美国已经悄然失去了对它们来源的控制。 一家成立两年的初创公司刚刚筹集了 3.1 亿美元来改变这一现状。

Mariana Minerals 不向矿工出售软件。 它宣布，它使用自己的人工智能堆栈自行拥有并运营这些矿山。 Khosla Ventures 领投 B 轮融资，a16z 和 Breakthrough Energy 回归。 据《财富》杂志率先报道，这使得该公司的总资本达到约 4 亿美元，估值为 15 亿美元。

创始人是一个不同寻常的组合。 首席执行官特纳·考德威尔负责管理特斯拉的金属和矿物团队。 他的联合创始人来自 Affirm 的机器学习部门和能源项目融资部门。 这种混合就是整个音调。 他们认为，融合采矿执行、软件和资本，你可以用平常一半的时间建造一座矿山。

铜、锂和中国问题

紧迫性在于地缘政治。 中国主导着全球矿业。 它加工了世界上 90% 的关键矿物。 对于手机和武器中的稀土磁铁，这一比例上升至 92%。 人工智能正在将金属需求推向前所未有的水平。 这种依赖现在已成为一个国家安全问题，而不仅仅是一个经济问题。

玛丽安娜的答案是两个美国网站。 Copper One 是马里亚纳去年购买的犹他州闲置矿场。 它在四个月内通过自主软件重新启动，并正朝着每年 50,000 吨精炼铜的目标前进。 德克萨斯州 Lithium One 的目标是从石油和天然气废水中提取电池级锂，计划于 2027 年实现产量。

铜就是答案。 它是电气化的瓶颈，而人工智能时代的电网正为此而紧张。 “如果没有国内供应链，你就无法引领人工智能世纪，”特拉维斯·卡兰尼克说。 这位前 Uber 老板现在经营着一家机器人公司。 将资金投入能源和电网硬件也是同样的逻辑。

软件无法挖坑

支持者名单就是信号。 除了 a16z 和 Khosla 之外，还有世界上最大的矿业公司之一必和必拓 (BHP) 以及中央情报局 (CIA) 的风险投资部门 In-Q-Tel。 这就是风险投资、工业和国家安全对同一个论点的押注。 谁以最快的速度实现采矿自动化，就有助于决定谁赢得人工智能的发展，以及谁继续依赖中国。

这种谨慎是与生俱来的。 这不是 SaaS。 建筑工人、加工厂和商品价格，这些都是软件无法变通的。 Copper One 仍需扩大现有业务规模。 Lithium One 仍需将全新设施投入商业生产。 两者都可能滑倒。

维诺德·科斯拉 (Vinod Khosla) 清楚地界定了这一差距。 矿物质就在那里；他说，缺失的部分是自主提取它们的意愿和人工智能。 Mariana 希望在十年内完成十个商业项目，每个项目都为下一个项目训练软件。 它是滑梯上的一个优雅的飞轮，但在地面上建造起来却非常困难。

目前，该论文的价值已确定为 15 亿美元。 证据不会以演示或演示形式出现。 它将按计划生产数吨铜和锂，成本将低于现有企业。 这是下一轮必须击败的数字。
